title: Vietnamese Caramel Pork with Eggs
equipment: heavy saucepan or small Dutch oven

qty.note: trimmed of silverskin, cut in 1 1/2-inch chunks
one 8.45-oz box; plain coconut water, not sweetened coconut juice with pulp

qty.unit: cup (2 tbsp for the caramel, the rest to loosen the sauce)

steps.text: Make the caramel: spread the brown sugar in a dry saucepan over medium heat and let it melt undisturbed for 4 minutes, then swirl in 2 tablespoons of the water until you have a deep amber syrup. Watch closely - it burns in seconds.
Add the oil, shallot, and garlic; stir 1 minute to soften in the syrup.
Add the pork chunks and turn to coat in the syrup; sear 3 minutes, turning once.
Pour in the fish sauce, coconut water, and the rest of the water, scraping the syrup loose from the bottom, and bring to a simmer.
Meanwhile boil the eggs: 9 minutes in salted water, then chill under cold running water and peel. Eggs are safe at 160°F (71°C) - at 9 minutes the yolks are just fully set.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Cover and simmer the pork gently for 25 minutes, stirring now and then. Pork is safe at 145°F (63°C) with a 3-minute rest, and a long simmer goes far past that - what you are watching for is the sauce turning brick-dark and glossy.

safety.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperature table

steps.text: Halve the eggs and nestle them in the sauce; simmer uncovered 5 minutes so they drink up color.
Cook the jasmine rice while the pot rests 5 minutes off the heat, then skim the fat from the sauce.
Serve the pork and eggs over rice with plenty of sauce, and finish with green onions and black pepper.
